title: PMDC MDCAT High-Yield Biology Foundation Test
instructions: Official PMDC MDCAT Assessment covering Biomolecules, Cell Structure, and Bioenergetics.
subject: Biology

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a reducing sugar possessing a free ketone or aldehyde group?
options: Sucrose
Maltose
Cellulose
Starch
questions.explanation: Maltose is a reducing disaccharide with a free aldehyde group. Sucrose is non-reducing because both anomeric carbons participate in the glycosidic bond.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The primary structural linkage that joins amino acids in a polypeptide chain is called:
options: Glycosidic bond
Phosphodiester bond
Peptide bond
Disulfide bridge
questions.explanation: Peptide bonds are covalent bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another with the release of water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which organelle is responsible for the packaging, modification, and sorting of secretory proteins?
options: Golgi apparatus
Lysosome
Peroxisome
Nucleolus
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins received from the rough ER, adds carbohydrates/lipids, and packages them into secretory vesicles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which cellular junction in animal tissues forms a tight seal that prevents fluid leakage between epithelial cells?
options: Desmosomes
Gap junctions
Tight junctions (zonula occludens)
Plasmodesmata
questions.explanation: Tight junctions form continuous water-impermeable barriers between adjacent epithelial cell membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In aerobic respiration, the terminal electron acceptor in the mitochondrial electron transport chain is:
options: NAD+
FAD
Molecular Oxygen (O2)
Cytochrome c
questions.explanation: Molecular oxygen accepts electrons at Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) and is reduced to form water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How many net molecules of ATP are generated directly by substrate-level phosphorylation during one turn of the citric acid cycle (per acetyl-CoA)?
options: 1 ATP / GTP
2 ATP
3 ATP
36 ATP
questions.explanation: One turn of the Krebs cycle produces 1 GTP (equivalent to 1 ATP) at the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which level of protein structure is characterized by alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets stabilized by hydrogen bonds?
options: Primary structure
Secondary structure
Tertiary structure
Quaternary structure
questions.explanation: Secondary structure consists of alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets formed by regular hydrogen bonding between peptide backbone atoms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The lysosomal membrane maintains an acidic internal lumen (pH ~4.5–5.0) via active transport carried out by:
options: Na+/K+ ATPase
Proton (H+) V-type ATPase pump
Calcium ATPase
Glucose symporter
questions.explanation: Vacuolar H+-ATPases continuously pump protons from the cytosol into the lysosomal lumen to maintain optimal pH for acid hydrolases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A competitive enzyme inhibitor acts by:
options: Binding permanently to the allosteric site
Binding reversibly to the active site, increasing Km without changing Vmax
Decreasing both Km and Vmax equally
Binding exclusively to the enzyme-substrate complex
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors resemble substrate and compete for the active site. They increase apparent Km (requiring more substrate), while Vmax remains attainable at high substrate concentrations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: During the depolarization phase of an action potential in a nerve fiber, there is rapid influx of which ion?
options: Potassium (K+)
Sodium (Na+)
Chloride (Cl-)
Calcium (Ca2+)
questions.explanation: Depolarization occurs when voltage-gated Na+ channels open rapidly, allowing Na+ ions to flood into the axon down their electrochemical gradient.
